titre: Full Stack Developer — Business Process Digitalisation
accroche: I turn processes that live in spreadsheets and Word templates into applications teams actually use every day. *Eight applications and websites I designed and shipped are live.*

lignes: Two of the company's core activities ran on shared spreadsheets and hand-copied Word templates: tender responses and recruitment. *I designed, built and shipped both replacement applications.*

On a tender, the deadline and scope of supply had to be found by hand in files running to hundreds of pages, some of them scanned. The tool finds them and *shows the exact passage it took them from* — all that is left is to confirm.
A file can no longer go out with a mandatory step missed: the path is locked, from the first document through to invoicing.

On the recruitment side, tracking and filing can no longer drift apart — moving a candidate forward files their folder automatically, and hiring documents are generated from templates instead of being copied.
*The HR team switched without changing a single habit* — the new tracker uses the exact columns of the spreadsheet it replaced, and exports to the same format.

entrees.titre: Hope Traders Academy — Freelance Full Stack Developer
lignes: *Three web products delivered end to end*, each with its own marketing site and its application: a course and membership platform, an activity journal, and a market analysis terminal.
Design, development, launch and follow-up: interface, data, subscription billing, transactional email and admin back office.
Each tool is run directly by the client, with no day-to-day technical involvement.

entrees.sousTitre: Contract work for Bailey Assurances, CRFPE, Interloc
lignes: Custom web applications for three clients: full development, from interface to database.
Brochure sites and online stores, built from designs supplied by the design teams; worked alongside design and marketing in an agile setup.
Carries a bid from the first document through to the invoice: intake of attachments, automated reading, enforced stages, and a dashboard of live opportunities.
*Built for non-technical users* — every screen carries its own instructions and a guided tour on first login.

entrees.titre: Recruitment — from stated need to the candidate's first day
lignes: Replaces a shared spreadsheet and folders filed by hand: applicant tracking, generation of hiring documents, automatic archiving.
GDPR-compliant — candidate data is flagged for review, then deleted automatically once its retention period ends.

entrees.sousTitre: Hope Traders Academy · site and application
lignes: Sign-up, subscription billing, content released in stages, messaging with the team, and an admin back office.
Runs in the browser and *installs on a phone* like a native app.

entrees.sousTitre: Hope Traders Academy · site and application
lignes: Imports an account's history and turns it into statistics, charts and a calendar; notebook and PDF report export.
An assistant reads back through the entries and *surfaces what keeps recurring* — the habits you repeat without seeing them.

entrees.sousTitre: Hope Traders Academy · site and application
lignes: Pulls together *five scattered public data sources* into a single read, across 67 tracked markets. Accounts, free trial, subscription, and alerts ahead of major releases.
An IT services company and an engineering consultancy: site structure, expertise pages, contact forms and load times.
*Custom templates rather than a stack of plugins* — both teams keep their own pages alive, without a developer.

questions: Le titre anglais dit « Business Process Digitalisation ». L'alternative plus recherchée par les recruteurs est « Digital Transformation » — moins précise, mais plus courante. Dis-moi si tu la préfères.
